articles.title: Spray-dried deep eutectic solvent of Olmesartan medoxomil to modulate solubility, bioavailability, and surface characteristics.
articles.abstract: Olmesartan medoxomil (OLM) is classified as a BCS class II antihypertensive, necessitating an innovative formulation strategy due to its poor aqueous solubility (∼7.75 μg/mL) and low oral bioavailability (∼26%). This study aimed to determine the efficacy of the DESs in improving the biopharmaceutical properties of OLM. Choline chloride (ChCl) was used as the hydrogen bond acceptor (HBA), and urea and glycerol as the hydrogen bond donors (HBDs). An optimized DES system with the appropriate molar ratios of ChCl: urea: glycerol, 1:2:2, exhibited a high solubilization ability of OLM (16.86 ± 0.14 mg/mL). The optimized DES with OLM was then solidified by spray drying with Neusilin® US2, a mesoporous inorganic adsorbent, to yield a free-flowing powder (S-DES 5). FTIR, DSC, PXRD, and SEM characterization confirmed the conversion of crystalline OLM to a molecularly dispersed state in the DES and demonstrated intermolecular hydrogen bonding by spectral shift. In the BET surface area analysis, the mesoporous structure of the SDES-5 showed an average pore diameter of 15.526 nm, pore volume of 0.1265 cm³/g, and a specific surface area of 32.598 m²/g, which indicated good conditions for drug adsorption and stabilization. In vitro dissolution studies showed that the drug release rate of S-DES was much higher, with 96.7% drug released after 60 min, while only 31.8% of the drug was released from pure OLM after 60 min. The oral bioavailability was increased by 2.4 fold in Sprague-Dawley rats, indicated by significantly higher Cmax (448.20 μg/mL) and AUC0-t (5985.435 μg.h/mL). Stability studies were conducted in accelerated conditions, showing a formulation resistance to changes according to the ICH short-term 6-month study. In a nutshell, the findings reported that spray dried DES systems using mesoporous carrier could be a promising and scalable method to modulate the solubility and oral bioavailability of poorly water-soluble drugs.

articles.title: Oral angiotensin-(1-7) formulation attenuates structural alterations in established emphysema and protects against subsequent allergic airway inflammation.
articles.abstract: AIMS: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease and asthma can coexist, increasing disease burden and complicating treatment. We investigated whether oral angiotensin-(1-7) [Ang-(1-7)] treatment initiated after emphysema establishment attenuates pulmonary structural alterations and protects against subsequent ovalbumin (OVA)-induced allergic airway inflammation. MATERIALS AND METHODS: C57BL/6 mice were randomly assigned to experimental groups with or without elastase-induced emphysema. Emphysema was induced by three weekly intratracheal instillations of porcine pancreatic elastase. The mice subsequently received an oral formulation of Ang-(1-7) one week later, for four weeks. Treatment was discontinued before the subsequent OVA sensitization and challenge. The groups were sensitized and challenged with either OVA or PBS. Lung morphometry, inflammation, collagen deposition, pulmonary Ang II levels, and gene expression were assessed. KEY FINDINGS: Elastase caused persistent alveolar enlargement and reduced septal density. Oral Ang-(1-7) attenuated these abnormalities. Treatment reduced elevated pulmonary angiotensin II levels and increased ACE2 mRNA expression in an independent emphysema experiment. OVA induced eosinophilic inflammation, airway remodeling, and increased inflammatory gene expression in emphysematous mice. Following the OVA challenge, previously treated emphysematous mice exhibited reduced pulmonary eosinophilia, inflammatory scores, epithelial thickening, and collagen deposition, alongside improved alveolar morphometry. Ang-(1-7) also decreased the gene expression of CD206, arginase-1, NLRP3, caspase-1, p53, and p16. These protective effects occurred without significant changes in OVA-specific IgE levels. SIGNIFICANCE: Oral Ang-(1-7) provided structural and anti-inflammatory benefits after establishing emphysema, with protection also evident following an allergic challenge despite treatment withdrawal before sensitization. These findings support prior modulation of the injured pulmonary microenvironment as a promising therapeutic strategy to limit allergic inflammation and airway remodeling in structurally compromised lungs.

articles.title: Prenatal melatonin regulates lung prostanoids expression in newborn sheep exposed to chronic hypoxia.
articles.abstract: Chronic hypoxia during pregnancy disrupts the balance of pulmonary vasoactive agents, altering prostanoid signaling and increasing the contractility of resistance arteries. This leads to elevated pulmonary arterial pressure and vascular resistance, ultimately resulting in pulmonary hypertension of the neonate (PHN). While prenatal melatonin is known to influence vascular tone, its specific impact on the neonatal pulmonary prostanoid system in hypoxic pregnancies remains unclear. This study aimed to determine the effects of third-trimester maternal melatonin administration on the cyclooxygenase and prostanoid pathways, and to evaluate its efficacy in reversing PHN in a high-altitude ovine model. In-vivo and ex-vivo pulmonary vascular function was evaluated in neonatal lambs gestated and born under chronic hypoxia. Furthermore, lung samples from 12-day-old lambs were analyzed using RT-PCR, Western blotting, and immunohistochemistry. The results demonstrate that prenatal melatonin actively modulates the pulmonary vascular function, and the prostanoids system, altering both the transcriptional and translational expression of specific prostanoids, as well as their spatial localization within pulmonary resistance arteries. However, despite this significant molecular and structural modulation, maternal melatonin treatment failed to reverse or clinically improve PHN in the offspring. These findings highlight the complexity of hypoxia-induced vascular remodeling and suggest that melatonin-driven prostanoid modulation alone is insufficient to overcome PHN, although it can improve some pulmonary function in neonates.

articles.title: CLAY MINERALS AS FUNCTIONAL INGREDIENTS OF CHITOSAN/PVA INKS FOR PRESSURE-ASISTED MICRO-SYRINGE 3D PRINTING OF MEDICAL DEVICES.
articles.abstract: Hydrogel-based formulations are promising platforms for chronic wound management since they maintain a moist environment and enable controlled drug delivery. The advancements in 3D printing (3DP) enables the development of medical devices and medicines based on polymers, but their low printability is a limitation to overcome. This study explores chitosan/PVA/clay hydrogels as inks for Pressure-Assisted Micro-syringe 3DP, focusing on the influence of different clay minerals. Chitosan (4% w/w), PVA (2.3% w/w) and triethanolamine (2% w/w) were the basic ingredients, while clays (0.45% w/w laponite, 0.9% w/w montmorillonite, 1.81% w/w sepiolite and halloysite) were added as functional ingredients. The addition of clays made the polymeric mixture printable: Laponite provided the highest printing resolution, sepiolite reported great reproducibility after post-printing and montmorillonite prevented filament collapsing most effectively. FTIR and XRD confirmed interactions among components, such as polymer/clay intercalation, which could explain the printability and compressive Young Modulus improvements. The stability of the printed devices in simulated fluid can be controlled by the type of clay, which can be predicted by the wetting angle of hydrogels. In vitro cytocompatibility studies revealed a cell viability > 90% in all cases, confirming their biocompatibility. This exploratory study demonstrates that clays can modulate the behaviour of polymer mixtures and optimize their 3DP performance, thus enabling the production of personalized and tunable medical devices and/or medicines.

articles.title: Prelimbic cortex CRHR1 regulates Parkinson's disease-related anxiety through a PrLGlu-avBNSTGABA-VTADA pathway.
articles.abstract: Anxiety is a common non-motor symptom of Parkinson's disease (PD). Due to the unclear mechanism, treatment becomes challenging and significantly impacts the quality of life of patients. Although corticotropin-releasing hormone receptor 1 (CRHR1) is abundantly expressed in the prelimbic cortex (PrL) and have been implicated in PD and anxiety, the role and mechanism of PrL CRHR1 in PD-related anxiety remain unclear. By combining neuropharmacological, chemogenetic, neuroanatomical, and molecular approaches, the present study were performed to investigate the role of PrL CRHR1 in PD-related anxiety and to explore its neural pathways. In this study, unilateral 6-hydroxydopamine lesions of the substantia nigra pars compacta (SNc) in male Sprague-Dawley rats induced anxiety-like behaviors and decreased CRHR1 expression in the PrL compared to sham rats. In sham and the lesioned rats, pharmacological blockade of PrL CRHR1 induced anxiety-like behaviors, whereas its activation produced anxiolytic-like effects, with both effects attenuated in the lesioned rats. CRHR1 blockade was accompanied by increased c-Fos expression in the anterior ventral bed nucleus of the stria terminalis (avBNST), while selective knockdown of CRHR1 in avBNST-projecting PrLGlu neurons similarly enhanced anxiety-like behaviors. Activation of the PrL-avBNSTGABA-ventral tegmental area (VTA) pathway or the avBNST-VTADA pathway induced anxiety-like behaviors, whereas inhibition of either pathway produced anxiolytic-like effects. Together, these findings suggest that PrL CRHR1 regulates PD-related anxiety, at least in part through the PrLGlu-avBNSTGABA-VTADA pathway, thereby providing new insights into the neural mechanisms underlying PD-related anxiety.

articles.title: Radiolabeling of ortho/meta-[123I]iodo-Hoechst for proof of direct DNA strand breaks assisted by molecular modeling studies.
articles.abstract: The use of Auger-Meitner electron-emitting radionuclides in particular has been intensively studied in recent decades, as their extremely short range in the nanometer range enables highly localized damage to DNA and other intracellular structures. Radionuclides such as 123I and 125I are ideal for such applications because they release dense cascades of low-energy electrons during their electron capture decay. In this work, Hoechst derivatives were radiolabeled with 123I using isotopic exchange reaction or lactoperoxidase method in order to develop a tool for direct DNA damage dependent on the activity. Optimized radiolabeling yielded molar activities of 27.5 MBq/nmol and 84.1 MBq/nmol for isotopic exchange and lactoperoxidase method, respectively. Molecular modeling studies revealed a closer and more rigid coordination for the iodine of ortho-iodo-Hoechst (oIH) within the DNA in comparison with meta-iodo-Hoechst (mIH). DNA studies revealed 2.5 123I radionuclides per DNA which accounts for at least one double-strand break after one half-life of 123I. Cell studies with PC3 cells corroborated these findings with 27-34× higher impact of cell toxicity for oIH in comparison to mIH. The radiolabeled Hoechst derivatives are now available as robust tool for quantification of DNA damage, and the computational studies provide structural insights into the mechanism underlying the observed differences in DNA-damaging activity.

articles.title: Cadmium sulfide nanoparticles exacerbate colitis via Faecalibaculum rodentium-mediated modulation of the indole-3-lactic acid-Th17 axis.
articles.abstract: With the increasing application of cadmium sulfide nanoparticles (CdS-NPs), their potential adverse effects on intestinal health have attracted growing attention. However, the impact of CdS-NPs exposure on inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) and the underlying mechanisms remain unclear. Here, we demonstrate that daily oral gavage exposure to 1 mg/kg CdS-NPs for 4 weeks or 11 weeks alone did not induce apparent colonic inflammation in healthy mice but exacerbated both acute and chronic DSS-induced colitis, as evidenced by severe weight loss, increased disease activity, colon shortening, tissue damage, and immune infiltration. Integrated gut microbiota profiling and metabolomic analysis revealed that CdS-NPs markedly reduced the abundance and tryptophan-metabolizing capacity of Faecalibaculum rodentium (F. rodentium), leading to impaired indole-3-lactic acid (ILA) production. F. rodentium administration significantly alleviated CdS-NPs-aggravated DSS-induced colitis and restored serum ILA levels, accompanied by suppression of Th17 responses. Consistently, exogenous ILA treatment attenuated intestinal inflammation and suppressed Th17/IL-17 responses in vivo and inhibited Th17 differentiation in CD4+ T cells in vitro. Collectively, our findings identify microbial tryptophan metabolism and IL-17 signaling as critical mediators of intestinal inflammatory sensitization associated with CdS-NPs exposure and highlight the F. rodentium-ILA axis as a potential intervention target for CdS-NPs-induced intestinal inflammation.

articles.title: Proteomic Remodeling and Altered Brain Energy Metabolic Homeostasis in TP53-Knockout Syrian Golden Hamsters.
articles.abstract: The tumor suppressor TP53 is a critical regulator of cell-cycle control, apoptosis, senescence, and cellular metabolism. However, its role in maintaining energy homeostasis in normal tissues, particularly in the brain, remains incompletely understood. In this study, proteomic profiling of brain, leukocytes, pancreas, and plasma from p53 knock-out (p53-/- ) Syrian Golden Hamsters (Mesocrecetus auratus) was investigated and compared with wild-type (WT) hamsters. We found a larger alternation in differentially expressed proteins in brain samples, while the pancreas showed a higher proportion of upregulated proteins. Functional enrichment analyses revealed significant changes in metabolic pathways, including oxidative phosphorylation and NAD(P)-binding processes. Notably, energy metabolism-associated pathways were predominantly downregulated in the brain of TP53-/- hamsters, involving candidate proteins Bcl2l1, Mta1, Nqo1, and Ube3a. Validation experiments confirmed dysregulated expression of these proteins at both transcript and protein levels, which is highly related to mitochondrial functions. ATP measurements further demonstrated unbalanced energy homeostasis in TP53-deficient brain tissue. The proteomic atlas of the p53-/- new animal model in this work provides a novel genetic and functional foundation for understanding the role of TP53 in mental disorders, which can be potentially significant for biological science and medicine.

articles.title: Design of a Kv1.3×CD25 bispecific antibody to preferentially inhibit activated T cells and ameliorate T-cell-driven colitis.
articles.abstract: Kv1.3 and CD25 regulate complementary aspects of T cell activation and expansion, and therefore are attractive targets for immunomodulation. Here, we designed and generated BsAb, an IgG-like bispecific antibody targeting Kv1.3 and CD25, by grafting a Kv1.3-blocking peptide Vm24 into the CDR3 of one heavy chain of the CD25 antagonist antibody basiliximab and incorporating a knob-into-hole Fc design for heterodimerization. BsAb retained the CD25 binding and anti-proliferative activities of basiliximab while obtaining Kv1.3 blocking functionality. In activated human T cells, BsAb showed enhanced cellular binding and stronger inhibition of T cell activation and proliferation than the mono-specific comparators. BsAb also preferentially bound CD25hiKv1.3hi and TEM-like T cell populations. In a human T cell-driven DSS-induced mouse colitis model, BsAb demonstrated greater efficacy in reducing disease severity, colonic inflammation, and circulating human T cells than the mono-specific antibodies of Kv1.3 and CD25. These results support dual Kv1.3×CD25 targeting as a promising strategy for selective modulation of pathogenic T cell responses in inflammatory diseases.

articles.title: Targeting DHODH Suppresses Melanoma Progression via Pyrimidine Depletion and Mitochondrial Dysregulation.
articles.abstract: Dihydroorotate dehydrogenase (DHODH), a rate-limiting enzyme in de novo pyrimidine biosynthesis, has emerged as a promising therapeutic target in oncology. However, the antitumor efficacy and underlying mechanisms of DHODH inhibitors in melanoma remain incompletely understood. Here, we characterize a novel DHODH inhibitor, ZP0946, and elucidate its anti-melanoma activity and molecular mechanisms. ZP0946 exhibited potent antiproliferative effects on melanoma cells and induced robust S-phase cell cycle arrest. Mechanistically, ZP0946 depleted intracellular pyrimidine pools, and exogenous uridine supplementation abrogated this antiproliferative effect. Mitochondrial functional assays revealed that ZP0946 impaired ATP production, depolarized mitochondrial membrane potential, increased the levels of reactive oxygen species, and reduced the oxygen consumption rate. Exogenous uridine supplementation reversed this mitochondrial dysfunction. In immunodeficient nude mouse xenograft models, ZP0946 significantly suppressed melanoma xenograft growth without inducing detectable toxicity. Notably, compared with immunodeficient tumor-bearing models, the antitumor efficacy of ZP0946 was superior in immunocompetent syngeneic models, with a tumor growth inhibition rate of 78.2%. This enhanced therapeutic effect was accompanied by reduced frequencies of myeloid-derived suppressor cells. Collectively, our findings reveal that DHODH inhibition by ZP0946 exerts dual anti-melanoma effects through pyrimidine depletion and mitochondrial dysfunction, providing a preclinical rationale for targeting DHODH with ZP0946 in melanoma therapy.

articles.title: Layer-by-layer machine learning-assisted hyperspectral imaging for at-line non-destructive drug content monitoring in 3D-printed medicine.
articles.abstract: Three-dimensional (3D) printing in pharmaceuticals offers unprecedented control to meet patient-specific needs. However, rapid and accurate non-destructive quality monitoring and final product checks remain a critical bottleneck. Near-infrared hyperspectral imaging (NIR-HSI) was combined with machine learning to estimate nadolol content in semi-solid extrusion (SSE) 3D-printed (3DP) tablets. Hyperspectral images were acquired after successive printed layers, and layer-averaged spectra were calibrated against the measured content by a reference HPLC method at the unit level. Twenty spectral preprocessing pipelines and eight regression algorithms were evaluated using batch-grouped cross-validation and independent external test batches at three concentrations. The selected model achieved an external RMSEP of 0.276% w/w (95% CI: 0.235-0.316, or 0.387 mg nadolol dose per unit), corresponding to 4.0% of the mean content (n = 108 test tablets). In comparison, the top-layer-only model performed similarly (RMSEP 0.272% w/w), whereas the first-layer-only model showed higher error (0.327% w/w), indicating that this approach provided earlier manufacturing information. The mean HSI-HPLC difference satisfied a pre-specified ± 5% equivalence criterion (TOST, p < 0.001), with a bias of - 0.039% w/w (or - 0.055 mg per unit), emphasizing the potential for batch-level content monitoring. Layer-stacking experiments showed contributions from the layer below the exposed layer. Shapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) attributed the largest contributions in this formulation-specific model to 1520-1560 nm, where nadolol shows a distinct band. Exploratory pixel-level prediction maps further provided visualization of model-estimated spatial variation for future quality screening. Overall, this study establishes an at-line NIR-HSI framework for non-destructive quantitative assessment during layer-by-layer 3DP manufacturing.

articles.title: Decoupling formulation composition and printed architecture to engineer drug release from direct powder extrusion 3D-printed Olaparib tablets.
articles.abstract: Olaparib (OLA), a BCS class IV poly(ADP-ribose) polymerase inhibitor, exhibits poor, solid-state-dependent aqueous solubility, complicating formulation design. This study investigated Direct Powder Extrusion (DPE) 3D printing to integrate solid-state engineering with geometry-controlled drug release. Five formulations (F1-F5) containing OLA (30% w/w) were produced by DPE using a hydroxypropyl-β-cyclodextrin (HP-β-CD) and Soluplus® core, with F2-F5 additionally incorporating colloidal silica, mannitol, polyethylene oxide (PEO), or PEO/polyethylene glycol (PEG) 4000, respectively, to modulate matrix properties and drug release. Powder X-ray Diffraction (PXRD) and DSC confirmed polymorph-independent amorphization of OLA following DPE processing. Dissolution studies and mathematical modelling revealed a formulation-dependent release profile, with F5 showing the highest cumulative drug release at 100% infill density. The consistent ranking observed in extruded filaments confirms the intrinsic role of formulation composition in drug release. Based on these results, F5 was also printed at 90%, 70%, and 50% infill and characterized by high-resolution micro-computed tomography (HR-µCT) to relate internal architecture to dissolution behavior. Lower infill produced larger pore networks and faster release: complete release was achieved within 8 h at 70% and 24 h at 90% infill. HR-µCT revealed a non-linear relationship between nominal infill and measured porosity, while open pore volume correlated linearly with mean dissolution time (R2 = 0.9973; p = 0.033). Amorphous state and drug content were maintained after 12 months of storage. These findings demonstrate that DPE enables simultaneous engineering of drug solid state, formulation, and architecture, with HR-µCT providing quantitative structural descriptors for rational optimization of 3D-printed dosage forms.

articles.title: Hyaluronic acid based codelivery vaccine enhances humoral immunity through active lymph node targeting.
articles.abstract: Efficient co-delivery of antigens and adjuvants to secondary lymphoid organs represents a pivotal challenge in subunit vaccine development, aiming to enhance immunogenicity while minimizing systemic side effects. Although various nanocarrier systems have been explored for lymphatic targeting, many rely on passive drainage or non-specific cellular uptake, lacking active targeting mechanisms for efficient lymph nodes (LNs) accumulation. Here, we constructed a lymph node targeting vaccine by covalently conjugating the SARS-CoV-2 S1 subunit and the TLR7/8 agonist 3 M-052 onto a hyaluronic acid (HA) scaffold, termed HA-3 M-052-S1. We systematically evaluated its binding to the lymphatic endothelial receptor LYVE-1, lymph node targeting efficiency, and immunogenicity in mice. Our results demonstrate that HA-3 M-052-S1 exhibited high-affinity binding to LYVE-1 and rapidly accumulated in draining lymph nodes (dLNs) within 4 h post-injection. The vaccine induced significantly higher frequencies of T follicular helper cells and germinal center B cells compared to alum-adjuvanted or simple mixture formulations. Moreover, it elicited potent and durable antigen-specific antibody responses, with neutralizing antibody titers substantially exceeding those of control groups. Importantly, the co-crosslinked vaccine conferred protection against SARS-CoV-2 challenge comparable to an adenoviral vector vaccine. This study establishes an active lymph node targeting strategy via HA-LYVE-1 interaction and provides a robust platform for next-generation subunit vaccines with enhanced potency and safety.

articles.title: Hyaluronic acid-grafted pH-responsive microcarriers for CD44-targeted co-delivery of Lactobacillus rhamnosus GG and its extrusion-derived bacterial membrane vesicles to rebalance intestinal homeostasis.
articles.abstract: Inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) stems from gut dysbiosis, impaired intestinal epithelial barriers and persistent mucosal immune dysfunction. Free oral probiotics or probiotic-derived extracellular vesicles yield poor therapeutic effects against IBD, as they degrade rapidly in the gastrointestinal tract and lack specific tropism for inflamed colon lesions. To overcome these delivery limitations, we fabricated pH-responsive hyaluronic acid (HA)-decorated alginate microcapsules (ALHA@LGG&EBMVs) to co-deliver viable Lactobacillus rhamnosus GG (LGG) and extrusion-derived bacterial membrane vesicles (EBMVs). The electrosprayed Ca2+-crosslinked alginate skeleton confers robust gastric-acid protection, and surface-immobilized HA enables specific binding to CD44 overexpressed on inflamed colon epithelium. In vitro simulated gastric fluid assays revealed that the ALHA shell afforded superior protection to encapsulated LGG and EBMVs. In vivo fluorescence tracing on dextran sulfate sodium-induced colitic mice showed ALHA@LGG&EBMVs achieved 2.7-fold higher cargo accumulation at inflammatory colon sites with 24 h prolonged lesion retention relative to untargeted cargo-loaded alginate microcapsules (AL@LGG&EBMVs). In vivo therapeutic assays verified that the dual-cargo microcapsules mitigated colitis symptoms, restored epithelial tight junctions and reduced excessive intestinal epithelial permeability. Mechanistic studies revealed concurrent improvements across three key pathological dimensions: balancing the abnormal Th17/Treg ratio, promoting anti-inflammatory M2 macrophage polarization, and remodeling dysbiotic gut microbiota to expand beneficial commensals and reduce the abundance of pro-inflammatory pathobionts, which collectively facilitate the restoration of intestinal homeostasis. This polysaccharide delivery system integrates gastric-acid shielding and active inflammatory-lesion targeting to achieve multi-dimensional restoration of intestinal homeostasis. This proof-of-concept study offers a biocompatible microecological nanomedicine prototype for IBD intervention and establishes a blueprint for the development of oral gut-targeted biomaterials.

articles.title: STING-inhibitor-phenamil polymeric nanocarriers for the in vitro modulation of macrophage polarization.
articles.abstract: Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) is a systemic autoimmune disease characterized by chronic inflammation and polyarthritis. RA has no cure and imposes a significant burden on individuals because current standard-of-care anti-inflammatory treatments reduce inflammation by regulating lymphocyte proliferation and pro-inflammatory cytokine function. However, recent studies have shown that macrophages play a pivotal role in the progression of RA and therefore, we hypothesize that co-loaded nanocarriers (NCs) containing a STING inhibitor and phenamil can reduce inflammation by repolarizing macrophages from a pro-inflammatory (M1-like) to an anti-inflammatory (M2-like) phenotype. Using Flash NanoPrecipitation (FNP), both compounds were encapsulated into polymeric nanocarriers which were then tested for their ability to induce an anti-inflammatory phenotype in vitro. Macrophage NF-κB activation levels were assessed using a reporter cell line, gene expression via qRT-PCR, and polarization state via flow cytometry. NF-κB activity was monitored using a cell line that secretes embryonic alkaline phosphatase upon activation; reductions in this signal indicate suppression of inflammatory signaling. Key markers examined for an anti-inflammatory phenotype for macrophages included IL-1β, IL-6, IL-10, and TGF-β. Finally, by assessing the ratio of M2-like to M1-like macrophages, we sought to determine if these formulations could successfully repolarize macrophages from M1-like to M2-like, and/or help macrophages resist polarization to an M1-like state following exposure to a pro-inflammatory stimulus. Through this work, we aimed to investigate how nanotechnology can be leveraged to improve therapeutic outcomes by regulating macrophage polarization states.

articles.title: The IgM- and IgA-enriched immunoglobulin preparation trimodulin suppresses neutrophil extracellular trap formation more effectively in vitro than standard intravenous immunoglobulin.
articles.abstract: Neutrophil extracellular traps (NETs) represent an important mechanism of defense against pathogens. However, in cases of severe lung infection or sepsis, excessive NET formation has been observed to cause vascular occlusion, inflammation, and tissue damage. Treatment with intravenous immunoglobulins (IVIg), especially those enriched for IgA and IgM, has been shown to improve outcomes in patients with these conditions. We compared trimodulin, a novel polyvalent antibody preparation containing elevated levels of IgM (∼23%) and IgA (∼21%), with standard IVIg to determine their ability to reduce NET formation in vitro. Trimodulin strongly reduced NET formation by neutrophils stimulated with phorbol 12-myristate 13-acetate (PMA), complexed IgA, or complexed IgG. This effect was accompanied by reduced IL-8 secretion. Standard IVIg showed no significant effect. Dissecting trimodulin into its individual immunoglobulin components revealed that IgM has the strongest capacity to reduce NET formation, followed by IgG. Nevertheless, the combined additive effects of the individual immunoglobulins were less effective than trimodulin, potentially caused by synergistic effects between the three immunoglobulin classes within trimodulin. Together, our data show that trimodulin is a more potent regulator of NET formation than the tested standard IVIg, mainly due to its IgM component. Therefore, trimodulin may be beneficial in conditions involving excessive NET formation.

articles.title: Elastin-based polypeptide-Fc fusion for extended subcutaneous exposure and sustained thrombopoietic activity.
articles.abstract: Immune thrombocytopenia is characterized by increased platelet destruction and impaired platelet production. Thrombopoietin receptor agonists (TPO-RAs) stimulate megakaryopoiesis, but the influence of elastin-based polypeptide (EBP) length on the hydrodynamic properties and platelet responses of Fc-fused TPO-RAs remains unclear. We generated three EBP-Fc fusion TPO-RAs-NT-202 G3, G6, and G12-and evaluated their physicochemical properties, biological activity, and platelet responses; G12 was also examined in an exploratory pharmacokinetic study. The variants, produced in Expi293 cells, differed only in EBP length; all remained soluble at 37°C in phosphate-buffered saline, and hydrodynamic size increased with EBP length. Binding was detected in BaF3/hMPL cells expressing the human thrombopoietin receptor but was minimal in parental BaF3 cells. The variants induced M-07e cell proliferation, JAK2-STAT signaling, and megakaryocytic differentiation of human CD34+ cells. After a single subcutaneous dose of 500 µg/kg in normal mice, platelet elevation persisted longest with NT-202 G12. At 2000 µg/kg, NT-202 G12 peaked at 72 h and remained quantifiable through 336 h. Because the pharmacokinetic study lacked an intravenous arm, used a different dose from the platelet-response studies, and relied on composite mean profiles, it was interpreted descriptively and could not distinguish absorption from elimination or establish an exposure-response relationship. In an anti-CD41 antibody-induced acute thrombocytopenia model, NT-202 G12 and romiplostim, an Fc-peptide TPO-RA, increased platelet counts without a significant between-group difference on day 9. Overall, this exploratory proof-of-concept study suggests that EBP block length is a genetically encoded design variable associated with hydrodynamic size and platelet-response duration.

articles.title: Enhanced mitochondrial respiratory metabolism in UV-damaged HDF cells based on metabolomics analysis of fermented Galla rhois gallnut extract.
articles.abstract: UV-induced photoaging disrupts mitochondrial homeostasis in skin cells, which in turn exacerbates skin aging. In this study, we developed a novel fermented Galla rhois gallnut extract (FGRE) using Lactiplantibacillus plantarum with mitochondrial respiratory homeostasis amelioration. Biochemical assays showed that FGRE exhibited stronger antioxidant and anti-elastase activities than the unfermented extract. Using Seahorse XF Cell Mito Stress Test, 1% FGRE significantly enhanced mitochondrial respiratory function in UVB-irradiated human dermal fibroblast (HDF) cells compared to that with the unfermented extract. In addition, 1% FGRE increased the ATP content and NAD+/NADH ratio and regulated the transcription level of fusion and fission genes in UVA-induced HDFs. Furthermore, the non-targeted metabolomics analysis revealed that differential metabolites were predominantly enriched in amino acid metabolic pathways, and 24 differential metabolites were putatively identified. Among these, the differential metabolites leucinic acid, urolithin A, and urolithin M5 were quantitatively determined. Notably, 1 μg/mL leucinic acid (equivalent to the concentration in 1% FGRE) ameliorated mitochondrial respiratory dysfunction and promoted the ATP production in UV-induced HDFs. Therefore, leucinic acid was considered as one of the potentially bioactive metabolites of FGRE.

articles.title: A retrospective case series and technological review of post-surgical analgesia for orthopedic surgery using a smart connected infusion pump: an opioid-sparing protocol.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Opioid-sparing analgesia (OSA) strategies aim to reduce perioperative opioid exposure while maintaining effective pain control. Continuous peripheral nerve blocks (cPNBs) supported by ambulatory infusion pumps have demonstrated efficacy in reducing opioid consumption, yet data on electronic infusion systems in the home environment remain limited. METHODS: A retrospective, single-center, uncontrolled feasibility series evaluated the performance of a smart connected electronic infusion pump within a multimodal opioid-sparing postoperative analgesia protocol in routine clinical practice. Twenty orthopedic surgery patients with continuous peripheral nerve catheters and patient-controlled boluses received an initial 20 mL nerve block (adductor canal, with or without supplemental iPACK, or interscalene/infraclavicular brachial plexus) followed by 0.2% ropivacaine via a standardized infusion regimen (8 mL/h basal rate with 3 mL patient-controlled bolus, 30-min lockout). RESULTS: Postoperative opioid consumption over 3 days varied by procedure type and regional anesthesia technique. Overall, a median of 15 MME (IQR: 0-39.4 MME, range: 0-90 MME). Shoulder surgery patients (n = 12, 60% of cohort) receiving interscalene brachial plexus catheters had a median consumption of 15 MME (IQR: 0-45 MME, range: 0-90 MME), with 42% (5/12) using no opioids. ACL reconstruction patients (n = 3, 15% of cohort) receiving adductor canal blocks had even lower consumption, with a median of 0 MME (range: 0-22.5 MME) and 67% (2/3) reporting no opioid use. Patients undergoing other procedures (TKA, PFL and humerus fracture; n = 4, 20% of cohort) had a median consumption of 41.25 MME (range: 7.5-52.5 MME), and the thumb surgery patient (5%) reported no opioid use. Seventeen patients (85%) completed the full programmed infusion; the remaining three (15%) discontinued early due to catheter dislodgement, not pump malfunction. All alarms were resolved at home without interrupting therapy, and no pump-related discontinuations occurred. CONCLUSION: In this small, real-world retrospective, single-center, uncontrolled feasibility series, a smart electronic infusion pump reliably delivered opioid-sparing perineural analgesia within a multimodal OSA protocol following orthopedic surgery in ambulatory and home settings, with no pump-related discontinuations and successful patient management of alarms. These observations support feasibility; analgesic adequacy was assessed only as a binary outcome (pain controlled or uncontrolled). Future comparative studies evaluating different ambulatory infusion platforms would help identify optimal device characteristics for home-based perineural analgesia.

articles.title: T-BET promotes inflammatory specialization without driving terminal maturation of iPSC-derived NK cells.
articles.abstract: Induced pluripotent stem cells (iPSCs) provide a scalable platform for off-the-shelf immune cell therapies; however, the mechanisms controlling maturation and functional specialization of iPSC-derived natural killer (iNK) cells are not fully understood. In this study, we combined single-cell transcriptomics, phenotypic profiling, and functional assays to characterize iNK cells and to determine whether temporally controlled expression of the transcription factor T-BET (TBX21) can promote iNK terminal specification and effector functions. Single-cell RNA sequencing and phenotypic profiling confirmed that baseline iNK cells form a transcriptionally distinct NK population and retain a developmental transcriptional signature. These iNK cells exhibited incomplete terminal maturation compared with peripheral blood NK cells, expressing much of the cytotoxic machinery but displaying limited acquisition of maturation-associated receptors. Despite induction of selected terminal specification markers, T-BET did not shift iNK cells toward a peripheral NK-like transcriptional identity. Instead, T-BET selectively triggered an inflammatory effector program characterized by elevated CCL3, CCL5 and GZMA expression and increased IFNγ production across multiple tumor targets, without enhancement of terminal cytotoxic gene programs. These findings suggest a functional dissociation between inflammatory and cytotoxic programs in iPSC-derived NK cells. This work highlights transcriptional engineering as a strategy to modulate functional state in stem cell-derived NK cells.

articles.title: Targeting IL-1R1 and androgen receptor using natural compounds from Aconitum heterophyllum and Podophyllum hexandrum: an in silico and in vitro study.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Lung and prostate cancers remain leading causes of cancer-related mortality worldwide, driven by inflammation-mediated tumour progression and hormone-dependent signalling. IL-1R1 promotes chronic inflammation, metastasis, and tumour survival, while androgen receptor (AR) signalling is a central driver of prostate cancer growth. Simultaneous targeting of inflammatory and androgenic pathways represents a promising strategy to overcome therapeutic resistance. OBJECTIVES: This study aimed to evaluate natural compounds derived from Aconitum heterophyllum (atisine, linoleic acid) and Podophyllum hexandrum (podophyllotoxin), as modulators of IL-1R1 and AR using integrated experimental and computational approaches. METHODS: Phytochemicals were extracted from tuberous roots of A. heterophyllum and fruits of P. hexandrum using Soxhlet extraction and isolated by TLC and column chromatography. Cytotoxicity and long-term antiproliferative effects were assessed using MTT and colony formation assays in A549 (lung) and LNCaP (prostate) cancer cell lines. Computational analyses included ADMET profiling, molecular docking against IL-1R1 (PDB: 1ITB) and AR (PDB: 2YHD), 100 ns molecular dynamics simulations, MM-GBSA binding free-energy calculations, network pharmacology-based target and pathway enrichment analyses. RESULTS: Podophyllotoxin exhibited potent cytotoxicity with IC50 values of 0.04 µM in both A549 and LNCaP cells, outperforming doxorubicin, while atisine showed moderate activity (IC50: 2.1-2.3 µM). Linoleic acid displayed weak anticancer activity (IC50 >100 µM). Colony formation assays confirmed strong suppression of clonogenic survival by podophyllotoxin and a moderate inhibitory effect by atisine. Docking studies suggested favorable binding affinities (-8.1 to -5.9 kcal/mol), and molecular dynamics simulations demonstrated stable protein-ligand complexes with low RMSD fluctuations. ADMET analysis supported favorable drug-likeness for atisine and podophyllotoxin. Network pharmacology identified 133 intersecting targets, with key hub genes including SRC, EGFR, and AKT1, enriched in PI3K-Akt and cancer-related signaling pathways. CONCLUSION: Atisine and podophyllotoxin exhibited significant anticancer activity and demonstrated favorable predicted interactions with the Interleukin-1 receptor type 1 (IL-1R1) and Androgen Receptor (AR), suggesting their potential as dual modulators that warrant further experimental validation. Their promising anticancer profile was supported by strong cytotoxicity, favorable predicted protein-ligand interactions, acceptable pharmacokinetic properties, and multitarget network pharmacology analyses. These findings provide a preliminary foundation for further optimization and in vivo validation toward the development of novel anticancer therapeutics targeting inflammation-driven and androgen-dependent cancers.

articles.title: Mechanism-driven nano-therapeutic platform integrating plant-derived compounds and membrane-active peptides reprograms inflammatory, cell cycle arrest, cGAS-STING, and apoptotic gene expression to quench colorectal cancer.
articles.abstract: Colorectal cancer (CRC) remains one of the leading causes of cancer-related mortality worldwide, and its first-line chemotherapeutic, 5-fluorouracil (5-FU), is constrained by poor tumor selectivity, dose-limiting systemic toxicity, and the frequent emergence of drug resistance. Nanocarrier-based co-delivery of naturally derived, multi-targeted agents offers a promising strategy to enhance efficacy while limiting off-target harm. This study evaluated the antitumor effects of nanoformulated liposomal melittin peptides (LIP-MLT) and niosomal chrysin (NsCR), administered as monotherapy or as combined therapy (LIP-MLT/NsCR), against DMH-induced CRC in a rat model. CRC was induced by subcutaneous injection of DMH (1,2-dimethylhydrazine, 40 mg/kg, twice weekly) for 8 weeks. Sprague-Dawley rats (n = 120) were randomly divided into six groups: healthy control (CON); untreated colorectal tumour (CR-TUM); and DMH-induced rats treated with 5-fluorouracil (CR-TUM + FU5), liposomal melittin (CR-TUM + LIP-MLT), niosomal chrysin (CR-TUM + NsCR), or the combination (CR-TUM + LIP-MLT/NsCR). Oxidant/antioxidant status, inflammatory cytokines, and the transcriptional profiles of inflammatory, cell-cycle-arrest, apoptotic/antiapoptotic, cGAS-STING innate-sensing, mTOR, and angiogenesis/metastasis genes were assessed, together with histopathological and immunohistochemical evaluation. The untreated CR-TUM group showed pronounced tumor-markers elevation, anemia, oxidative damage, and a strong pro-inflammatory, immunosuppressive shift. Relative to CR-TUM, LIP-MLT/NsCR lowered the tumor markers CEA (3.1-fold), CA19-9 (3.5-fold), and CCSA (2.1-fold), and reduced the oxidative markers ROS (2.2-fold), MDA (1.8-fold), and NO (2.2-fold) while raising the antioxidants. It also decreased the pro-inflammatory mediators NF-κB (2.3-fold), IL-1β (2.4-fold), and TNF-α (1.7-fold) versus CR-TUM, reversing approximately 71% of the DMH-induced inflammatory signature. At the transcriptional level, the combination produced the strongest upregulation of the pro-apoptotic genes (Caspase-3, Caspase-8, BAX, and p53) with concurrent downregulation of the antiapoptotic mediators (Bcl-2, c-FLIP, and Survivin), and marked proliferative and metastatic drivers suppression, including CDK4, CDK6, cyclin D1, β-catenin, mTOR, MMP-9, and VEGF, alongside restoration of the CDK inhibitors p21, p27, and KLF4 and normalization of cGAS, STING, and IRF3 mRNA levels. LIP-MLT/NsCR further best-preserved body weight and colon length, lowered diarrhea and rectal-bleeding scores, restored colonic histopathological architecture, and most strongly diminished the immunoexpression of MMP-9 and VEGF relative to untreated cancer tissues. Taken together, the combined LIP-MLT/NsCR nanoformulation attenuated DMH-induced CRC progression to a greater extent than either monotherapy or conventional 5-FU, supporting the combined melittin-chrysin nanoformulation as a promising, multi-targeted strategy against colorectal cancer.

articles.title: Cost-effectiveness of inavolisib plus palbociclib/fulvestrant versus palbociclib/fulvestrant for PIK3CA-mutated advanced breast cancer in China.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Based on the positive findings of the INAVO120 study, inavolisib is the only phosphatidylinositol 3-kinase alpha (PI3Kα) inhibitor approved for breast cancer treatment in China and has been included in the National Reimbursement Drug List following national medical insurance price negotiations. METHODS: A partitioned survival model with a 30-year time horizon was constructed to assess the cost-effectiveness of inavolisib plus palbociclib/fulvestrant versus palbociclib/fulvestrant alone in patients with phosphatidylinositol-4,5-bisphosphate 3-kinase catalytic subunit alpha (PIK3CA)-mutated, hormone receptor (HR)+, human epidermal growth factor receptor 2 (HER2)-, locally advanced or metastatic breast cancer (a/m BC). Clinical data were extracted from the Asian cohort of the INAVO120 trial. Drug prices were sourced from the government procurement platform, while additional cost and utility parameters were derived from the published literature. The primary model outcome was the incremental cost-effectiveness ratio (ICER). To assess the robustness of the results, scenario and sensitivity analyses were performed. Additionally, a price simulation analysis was conducted for inavolisib. RESULTS: The ICER was determined to be $36,932.91/quality-adjusted life-year (QALY), which exceeded the willingness-to-pay (WTP) threshold of $27,906/QALY. To attain cost-effectiveness, a further price reduction of 27.02% for inavolisib would be necessary. Scenario and sensitivity analyses confirmed the robustness of the results. CONCLUSION: The addition of inavolisib to palbociclib plus fulvestrant for PIK3CA-mutated HR+/HER2-a/m BC is not a cost-effective treatment strategy at the national level in China. However, this triple therapy may achieve cost-effectiveness in economically affluent regions with higher local WTP thresholds.

articles.title: Antiprotozoal drug exposure and reduced long-term mortality and morbidity: a multi-cohort pharmacoepidemiologic study.
articles.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Medications may affect age-related morbidity and overall survival beyond their original indications. Systematic identification of such effects may inform drug repurposing strategies for healthy aging. We aimed to identify medications associated with longevity and reduced age-related morbidity using large-scale electronic health record data. METHODS: We conducted a stepwise pharmacoepidemiologic investigation in two independent healthcare systems. Using electronic health records from a nationwide health provider, we performed an exploratory medication-wide case-control screen comparing medication exposure during a 10-year window between 14,986 individuals who died before sex-specific median life expectancy and matched controls who survived beyond their life expectancy. Two leading candidate drugs, atovaquone-proguanil and mefloquine, are antiprotozoal agents with activity against Toxoplasma gondii. Their effects on mortality and age-related morbidity were further evaluated within a historical cohort of 3,876 exposed individuals and 77,520 matched controls using Cox proportional hazards models adjusted for baseline characteristics. External validation was performed in the United States-based TriNetX network, including cohorts exposed to atovaquone-proguanil (n = 24,498), mefloquine (n = 3,400), and nirmatrelvir-ritonavir (n = 124,681), each matched to unexposed controls. RESULTS: Atovaquone-proguanil and mefloquine, together with nirmatrelvir-ritonavir, a protease inhibitor with reported antiprotozoal effects, were associated with consistent reductions in all-cause mortality across cohorts and lower incidence of multiple age-related conditions, including dementia, diabetes mellitus, cardiovascular disease, chronic kidney disease, and selected malignancies. Consistent increases in specific conditions were also observed, including hearing loss, Sjögren's syndrome/dry eye, and lichen planus, suggesting shared underlying mechanisms, although confounding cannot be excluded. DISCUSSION: Findings were consistent across healthcare systems and drug classes, including in populations exposed to non-travel-associated medications. While causality cannot be established, these results support further investigation into potential links between chronic protozoal infections and aging-related diseases.

articles.title: Magnolol alleviates high-fat diet-induced steatosis, inflammation and fibrosis in obesity-associated liver injuries via MOGAT1-mediated lipid metabolism and NF-κB signaling.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Magnolol (MAG), a bioactive compound from Magnolia officinalis, possesses anti-inflammatory and lipid-lowering properties, but its role in obesity-associated liver injury and its molecular targets remain unknown. METHODS: High-fat diet (HFD)-fed mice were treated with MAG (10 or 20 mg/kg) daily for 7 days. AML12 hepatocytes were challenged with PA with or without MAG pretreatment. Liver injury was evaluated by histology, serum biochemistry, qPCR and Western blot. RNA-seq and mechanistic studies were performed to identify MAG-regulated pathways and targets. RESULTS: MAG significantly reduced hepatic lipid accumulation, serum transaminases, and collagen deposition in HFD-fed mice. RNA-seq identified monoacylglycerol O-acyltransferase 1 (MOGAT1) as the most significantly downregulated lipogenic gene by MAG. MOGAT1 expression correlated positively with liver triglyceride and injury markers. MAG also suppressed HFD-induced NF-κB activation (reduced P65 phosphorylation and nuclear translocation, lower IL-6, TNF-α, IL-1β). These findings were recapitulated in PA-treated AML12 cells. Critically, MOGAT1 overexpression largely reversed MAG-mediated suppression of inflammatory and fibrotic responses, demonstrating a causal role of MOGAT1 in MAG's protective effects. CONCLUSION: MAG alleviates HFD-induced hepatic steatosis, inflammation and fibrogenic responses by suppressing MOGAT1-mediated triglyceride synthesis and subsequent NF-κB-driven inflammation. This study identifies MOGAT1 as a novel downstream effector and functional mediator of MAG, providing new mechanistic insight into its hepatoprotective action and supporting its therapeutic potential for obesity-associated liver injuries.

articles.title: Zang-Si-Wei and its core constituent ellagic acid alleviate LPS-induced acute lung injury by modulating PI3K/AKT signaling and NLRP3-associated pyroptosis.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Acute lung injury (ALI) is a life-threatening respiratory condition characterized by uncontrolled pulmonary inflammation and epithelial barrier dysfunction. Zang-Si-Wei Qingfei Mixture (ZSW) is a promising Tibetan herbal formula used clinically to alleviate pulmonary symptoms, yet its pharmacological targets and therapeutic pathways in ALI have not been fully explored. This study aims to identify the bioactive constituents of ZSW and elucidate their protective and therapeutic mechanisms in ALI. METHODS: ZSW's components were identified via liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry (LC-MS/MS) previously and network pharmacology. Target affinity was evaluated using molecular docking and molecular dynamics simulations. In vivo, C57BL/6J mice with lipopolysaccharide (LPS)-induced ALI were used to evaluate the pretreatment and post-treatment effects of ZSW and its core component, Ellagic Acid (EA). In vitro, MLE-12 cells and the PI3K/mTOR dual inhibitor BEZ235 were utilized to investigate the role of PI3K/AKT signaling and NLRP3 inflammasome activation and pyroptosis. RESULTS: EA was identified as ZSW's core bioactive constituent, demonstrating high binding stability with AKT1, PIK3CA, and PIK3R1. In vivo, ZSW and EA significantly attenuated lung histological damage, edema, and alveolar-capillary hyperpermeability. Both markedly reduced pro-inflammatory cytokines (TNF-α, IL-6 and IL-1β) in bronchoalveolar lavage fluid. Mechanistically, ZSW and EA inhibited PI3K and AKT phosphorylation and were accompanied by decreased NLRP3 inflammasome-associated proteins (decreased NLRP3, ASC, and cleaved Caspase-1) and GSDMD-mediated pyroptosis (decreased GSDMD-N and lactate dehydrogenase release). Notably, the 6-h post-LPS therapeutic model showed that both treatments effectively reversed established lung injury. CONCLUSION: ZSW and EA exert anti-inflammatory and lung-protective effects, accompanied by modulation of PI3K/AKT signaling and suppression of NLRP3 inflammasome-associated pyroptosis. This provides robust scientific evidence for ZSW's clinical application and highlights EA as a promising therapeutic candidate for acute inflammatory lung diseases.

articles.title: Isoallolithocholic acid attenuates acute liver allograft rejection by promoting Treg differentiation through the NR4A1/FOXP3 signaling axis.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Acute allograft rejection driven by disordered CD4+ T cell alloimmunity severely limits long-term graft survival following orthotopic liver transplantation (OLT). Conventional broad-spectrum immunosuppressants cause severe systemic side effects, while therapeutic approaches relying on metabolites to induce transplant tolerance remain insufficiently explored. Isoallolithocholic acid (isoallo-LCA), a secondary bile acid produced by gut microbiota, maintains Treg homeostasis, yet its biological function and molecular mechanisms in regulating hepatic alloimmune rejection have not been clarified. OBJECTIVE: To systematically explore the therapeutic efficacy of isoallo-LCA against acute liver allograft rejection and uncover its underlying molecular regulatory mechanism. METHODS: An MHC-mismatched murine orthotopic liver transplantation acute rejection model was established. Recipient survival, liver pathological injury, BANFF rejection scores and serum hepatic injury indicators (ALT, AST, TBIL) were detected to evaluate the protective effect of isoallo-LCA. Flow cytometry was applied to analyze intrahepatic Th1 and Treg proportions. Transcriptomic sequencing combined with in vivo and in vitro western blot assays was used to screen and verify key signaling molecules, and an NR4A1 inhibitor was administered to conduct rescue validation experiments. RESULTS: Isoallo-LCA intervention significantly prolonged recipient survival, alleviated intrahepatic inflammatory damage, lowered BANFF rejection grades and decreased serum ALT, AST and TBIL levels. Isoallo-LCA inhibited the differentiation of pro-inflammatory T-bet+ Th1 cells and promoted the expansion of FOXP3+ Tregs, restoring the balance of intrahepatic CD4+ T cell subsets. NR4A1 was identified as the core downstream effector of isoallo-LCA. Blockade of NR4A1 pharmacologically nearly eliminated the protective phenotypes mediated by isoallo-LCA, confirming the essential role of the NR4A1/FOXP3 signaling pathway. CONCLUSION: Isoallo-LCA relieves acute liver allograft rejection by activating the NR4A1/FOXP3 signaling axis to remodel intrahepatic Th1/Treg immune balance. These findings provide preclinical evidence supporting gut microbial bile acid metabolites as potential low-toxic adjuvant candidates for inducing transplant immune tolerance, although clinical translation requires further validation in human studies.

articles.title: Clinical effectiveness of mavacamten on cardiac function and disease-related indicators in patients with obstructive hypertrophic cardiomyopathy.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to compare the clinical effects of mavacamten and conventional pharmacotherapy on cardiac function and related disease indicators in patients with obstructive hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (oHCM). METHODS: A retrospective analysis was performed in patients with oHCM who were hospitalized between January 2024 and May 2025. The intervention group included 126 patients who received mavacamten for the first time, while the control group consisted of 134 patients treated with conventional medications. Baseline clinical characteristics, laboratory parameters, and imaging findings were collected. All patients were followed up for 30 weeks after discharge. Changes in relevant clinical indicators were recorded and compared at weeks 6 (W6), 18 (W18), and 30 (W30). RESULTS: A total of 222 patients (111 per group) completed the 30-week follow-up and were included in the final analysis. After 30 weeks of treatment, the resting left ventricular outflow tract (LVOT) peak gradient fell to 23.76 ± 4.09 mmHg in the intervention group but persisted at 78.49 ± 13.21 mmHg in the control group (t = 24.074, p < 0.001). Similarly, the Valsalva-provoked LVOT peak gradient decreased to 48.95 ± 11.10 mmHg versus 113.59 ± 14.92 mmHg in the control group (t = 21.147, p < 0.001). Left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) was 55.12% ± 4.85% in the intervention group and 56.78% ± 5.42% in the control group (p = 0.312), with 9.5% of mavacamten-treated patients experiencing LVEF decline to <50% (vs. 2.2% in controls). N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide (NT-proBNP) and high-sensitivity cardiac troponin I (hs-cTnI) levels were significantly lower in the intervention group (p < 0.05). CONCLUSION: Mavacamten indicates significant clinical association with improved outcomes in improving cardiac function and related disease indicators in patients with obstructive hypertrophic cardiomyopathy, with sustained reductions in both resting and provoked LVOT gradients.

articles.title: To chat or not to chat: how osteopathic students utilize artificial intelligence platforms in pharmacology education.
articles.abstract: INTRODUCTION: The rapid development of artificial intelligence (AI) tools has led to their expanding use in academia, medicine, and medical education. However, the quality, accuracy, source reliability, and integration of osteopathic principles in AI-generated content for pharmacology education remain insufficiently explored. Our goals were to use AI tools to generate pharmacology content, which we could critically evaluate for quality and accuracy, while exploring the capabilities and limitations of the outputs. The content we asked AI to generate was based on pharmacologically important concepts for osteopathic physicians in training, with the application of osteopathic philosophy included in some of the queries. METHODS: Three leading AI platforms, namely, Consensus Deep, Perplexity Pro, and ChatGPT Plus, were evaluated using three pharmacologically relevant queries. Each query was input into each platform, and the outputs were evaluated for quality, credibility, and source validity. The AI platforms we used required a paid subscription. RESULTS: Our results showed that Consensus Deep consistently provided output that included peer-reviewed journals and integrated osteopathic principles into its responses. Perplexity Pro provided information with references; several references included websites or social media posts, and when the prompt was refined and repeated, the output was limited and required additional purchase for further usage. ChatGPT Plus provided output which was patient-centered; when prompted for references, it provided references which had to be assessed for quality or credibility. DISCUSSION: Our study results indicate that generative AI platforms are a very useful tool for pharmacology and osteopathic medical education, although the use of the AI-generated content requires learners to critically evaluate the outputs for integrity, quality, and accuracy. In addition, there are currently limited data across AI platforms that include osteopathic principles and philosophy in pharmacology and therapeutics, and future work should be directed toward increasing scholarly research and publications in the fields of osteopathic medicine, pharmacology learning, and AI use.

articles.title: Cost-effectiveness analysis of ivonescimab plus chemotherapy in advanced squamous NSCLC: a Chinese healthcare system perspective with U.S. pricing scenario exploration.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Ivonescimab plus chemotherapy shows outstanding efficacy for advanced squamous non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), but its pharmacoeconomic value remains to be determined. Therefore, this study seeks to evaluate the cost-effectiveness of the ivonescimab regimen for advanced squamous NSCLC from the Chinese and U.S. healthcare perspectives, and to explore the theoretical cost-effective price threshold of ivonescimab. METHODS: Survival curves from the HARMONi-6 trial were fitted and extrapolated, and direct medical costs were calculated. A partitioned survival model was developed within TreeAge Pro to project disease trajectory and resource utilization over a 10-year time horizon. The primary outcome was the incremental cost-effectiveness ratio (ICER), compared against willingness-to-pay (WTP) to assess the ivonescimab regimen's cost-effectiveness. Sensitivity, scenario, and threshold analyses were performed to assess parameter uncertainty and estimate ivonescimab's theoretical cost-effective price threshold. RESULTS: In China, the ivonescimab group cost $60,942 for 2.33 QALYs versus $30,093 for 1.57 QALYs in the tislelizumab group, yielding an ICER of $40,328/QALY. Utility during progressive disease was the most influential parameter. Ivonescimab's theoretical cost-effective price thresholds were $27.85/100mg, $67.63/100mg, and $107.4/100mg, corresponding to WTPs of single, double, and triple the per-capita GDP, respectively. In the U.S., the total costs were $572,981 and $419,922, and the health outcomes were 3.16 QALYs and 2.19 QALYs for the two arms, with an ICER of $157,444/QALY. Ivonescimab's price was the dominant driver of ICER. The theoretical cost-effective price thresholds were $609.10/100 mg and $777.31/100mg, corresponding to the $100,000/QALY and $150,000/QALY WTP, respectively. CONCLUSION: Under the unified model framework of this study, compared with the tislelizumab regimen, the ivonescimab regimen as the first-line treatment for advanced squamous NSCLC in both countries is unlikely to have a cost-effectiveness advantage.

articles.title: Dual-scaffold imageable embolic system with microenvironment normalization enhances hypoxia-activated chemoembolization for HCC.
articles.abstract: Transarterial chemoembolization (TACE) for hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is limited by the post-embolization tumor microenvironment (pE-TME), which drives revascularization and fibrosis, thereby narrowing the hypoxic window and restricting drug penetration for hypoxia-activated prodrugs like tirapazamine (TPZ). To overcome this challenge, we developed a dual-scaffold theranostic platform integrating an iodinated thermosensitive PNIPAM hydrogel with genipin-crosslinked albumin microspheres for the coordinated co-delivery of nintedanib (NIB) and TPZ. This platform provides intrinsic X-ray visibility, rapid in situ gelation, enhanced mechanical strength, and sustained drug release with excellent hemocompatibility. In vitro, released NIB inhibited fibroblast proliferation, while TPZ potently induced apoptosis in hypoxic HCC cells. In vivo, the platform enabled stable vascular occlusion and prolonged tumor retention. In an orthotopic HCC model, the dual-drug combination achieved 91% tumor inhibition, significantly outperforming embolization alone and single-drug groups, without systemic toxicity. Mechanistically, TPZ promoted apoptosis (Caspase-3/Ki-67), whereas NIB suppressed compensatory angiogenesis (VEGF/CD31) and collagen deposition (α-SMA), thereby remodeling the pE-TME to stabilize hypoxia. By converting the therapy-limiting hypoxic microenvironment into a therapeutic asset, this dual-scaffold strategy offers a new paradigm for amplifying TACE efficacy.

articles.title: Natural Polymer-Based Mucoadhesive Patches for Cancer Therapy: Current Advances and Future Perspectives.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVE: The aim of the review is to discuss about natural polymer-based mucoadhesive patches for localized drug delivery in cancer therapy. It explains the various formulation techniques used in patch formulation, along with the principle and mechanism of mucoadhesion, evaluation parameters, and therapeutic uses in cancer. The available preclinical evidence is critically evaluated for benefits, limitations, translation challenges, and stronger evidence of therapeutic efficacy and safety in the recent literature prior to 2026. SIGNIFICANCE: Mucoadhesive Drug Delivery Systems (MDDS) uses mucoadhesive polymer that adhere to the mucosal wall and provide prolonged release of the drug, which results in higher bioavailability, and decreased hepatic first pass metabolism. Among the various dosage forms, the MDDS Patch gives close contact with the mucosa because they are able to interact with each other via various types of bonds, and polymer chain interpenetration. According to various literature surveys, natural polymers are biocompatible and biodegradable and exhibit excellent mucoadhesive properties, which can be exploited to create flexible patches to suit patient needs. KEY FINDINGS: The work incorporated in this review shows that natural polymers used to formulate mucoadhesive patches can deliver extended drug release, increase drug bioavailability, improve therapeutic efficacy, and enable focused drug delivery with enhanced patient compliance. CONCLUSIONS: Polymer-based mucoadhesive patches based on natural polymers are promising vehicles in localized drug delivery to treat cancer, which may offer an extended residence time, sustained drug delivery and availability in the local site.

articles.title: Physiologically Based Pharmacokinetic Modeling of Fruquintinib and Its Metabolite to Assess Drug-Drug Interaction Liability as an Object or Precipitant.
articles.abstract: Fruquintinib is approved, including in the United States and Europe, for previously treated metastatic colorectal cancer, regardless of biomarker status. Using in vitro and clinical data, physiologically based pharmacokinetic (PBPK) models were developed for fruquintinib and M11, a major metabolite of fruquintinib. The models were applied to evaluate the potential impact of strong/moderate/weak cytochrome P450 (CYP) and 3A4 (CYP3A4) inhibitors and inducers on the pharmacokinetics of fruquintinib and M11. In addition, the PBPK models were applied to evaluate the potential for P-glycoprotein or breast cancer resistance protein (BCRP)-mediated drug-drug interactions, with fruquintinib and M11 as precipitants (inhibitors). The simulations indicated that the changes in plasma exposure of fruquintinib area under the curve (AUC) geometric mean ratio (GMR) during administration with strong/moderate/weak inhibitors of CYP3A4 are negligible (< 1.25), and M11 interactions are weak with strong inhibition. Simulated changes in plasma exposure of fruquintinib in the presence of rifampin (a strong CYP3A4 and moderate CYP2C9 inducer) were > 0.20, but ≤ 0.50 (no significant change in M11). Fruquintinib AUC GMRs were > 0.50, but ≤ 0.80 with moderate CYP3A4 inducers, while the ratio fell between > 0.80 and 1.00 in the presence of weak CYP3A4 inducers. The effects of fruquintinib on the pharmacokinetics of P-glycoprotein or BCRP substrates were not clinically significant. These analyses support avoiding concomitant use of strong, and if possible, moderate CYP3A4 inducers with fruquintinib. In addition, no dose adjustments for fruquintinib are required in the presence of CYP3A4 inhibitors, or for medications that are substrates of P-glycoprotein or BCRP when used concomitantly with fruquintinib.

articles.title: An engineered pneumolysin ΔA146 derivative induces apoptosis in breast cancer cells: an in vitro proof-of-concept for antibody-drug conjugate payload development.
articles.abstract: The therapeutic potential of antibody-drug conjugates (ADCs) is frequently undermined by the emergence of resistance to conventional payloads, which predominantly exert their effects through the disruption of intracellular targets such as microtubules or nuclear DNA. In pursuit of therapeutic agents capable of bypassing these established resistance pathways, we turned our attention to the engineered bacterial pore-forming toxin, pneumolysin ΔA146 (PLY ΔA146). To evaluate its intrinsic cytotoxic potential independent of antibody-mediated delivery, we generated a recombinant fusion protein (CPP-PLY ΔA146) for direct cellular assessment. This construct demonstrated proficient cellular internalization into both HER2-positive SK-BR-3 and triple-negative MDA-MB-231 breast cancer cell lines. Subsequent functional analysis revealed a potent and concentration-dependent suppression of cell proliferation, yielding half-maximal inhibitory concentrations (IC₅₀) of approximately 1.140 µM and 1.433 µM, respectively, after a 72-hour exposure. Mechanistically, the observed cytotoxicity was fundamentally linked to the induction of programmed cell death. This was substantiated by a convergence of evidence: a significant elevation in Annexin V-positive populations, conclusive detection of DNA strand breaks, the cleavage and consequent activation of caspase-8 and caspase-3 along with a corresponding increase in their catalytic activities, a decisive shift in the Bax/Bcl-2 equilibrium toward a pro-apoptotic phenotype. Collectively, these results delineate a defined and efficacious pro-apoptotic mechanism for PLY ΔA146, one that is functionally discrete from the modalities of current ADC mainstays. These results provide an in vitro proof-of-concept for PLY ΔA146 as a potential candidate payload for future ADC development, proposing a strategic avenue to surmount existing limitations and potentially augment the efficacy of targeted oncological interventions.

articles.title: Biomimetic Platelet Membrane-Coated PLGA Nanoparticles for Enhanced Zingerone Delivery in Experimental Rheumatoid Arthritis.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVE: To develop and evaluate platelet membrane-coated poly (lactic-co-glycolic acid) (PLGA) nanoparticles encapsulating zingerone for targeted delivery and enhanced therapeutic efficacy against experimental rheumatoid arthritis. SIGNIFICANCE: Rheumatoid arthritis is a chronic inflammatory disorder characterized by synovial inflammation, oxidative stress, and progressive cartilage and bone destruction, resulting in pain, disability, and impaired mobility. Existing therapies often provide incomplete disease control and may cause systemic adverse effects, necessitating the development of safer and more effective targeted treatment strategies. METHODS: Zingerone-loaded PLGA nanoparticles were prepared and coated with platelet membranes to improve targeting of inflamed tissues. Physicochemical characterization included particle size, zeta potential, transmission electron microscopy, and spectroscopic analyses. Therapeutic efficacy was assessed in Freund's complete adjuvant-induced arthritic rats using clinical evaluation, cytokine quantification, antioxidant assessment, histopathology, radiography, and toxicity studies. RESULTS: Optimized ZP nanoparticles exhibited a mean hydrodynamic diameter of 134.35 ± 52.21 nm, which increased to 148.88 ± 69.35 nm following platelet membrane coating (PZP), indicating successful surface modification. Transmission electron microscopy demonstrated a spherical core-shell morphology, while spectroscopic analyses confirmed successful encapsulation without evidence of chemical incompatibility. Entrapment efficiency was 81.0 ± 1.0% for ZP and 81.7 ± 0.6% for PZP. Treatment significantly reduced paw edema (P < 0.001), arthritis scores, TNF-α, and IL-1β (P < 0.05), improved antioxidant status, preserved joint architecture, and produced no significant hepatic or renal toxicity. CONCLUSIONS: Platelet membrane-coated PLGA nanoparticles effectively enhanced zingerone delivery and anti-inflammatory activity, demonstrating considerable potential as a targeted nanotherapeutic platform for the management of rheumatoid arthritis.

articles.title: Comparing Length of Argatroban Use Among Patients Managed With Warfarin Versus Apixaban or Rivaroxaban for the Treatment of Suspected Heparin-Induced Thrombocytopenia.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: There is limited available data directly comparing warfarin versus direct oral anticoagulants (DOACs) for the treatment of acute or suspected heparin-induced thrombocytopenia (HIT). In addition, there are no studies assessing the difference in duration of parenteral anticoagulation when switched to a DOAC versus warfarin in this setting. OBJECTIVE: The purpose of this study is to determine if transitioning to rivaroxaban or apixaban versus warfarin is associated with a shorter duration of argatroban administration. METHODS: This single-center retrospective chart review included adults with suspected or acute HIT treated with argatroban and transitioned directly to warfarin, apixaban, or rivaroxaban. The primary outcome was duration of argatroban therapy. Secondary outcomes included hospital length of stay, bleeding events, new or recurrent thrombosis, and survival to discharge. RESULTS: Seventeen patients in the apixaban and rivaroxaban group and 27 patients in the warfarin group were included. Patients transitioned to apixaban or rivaroxaban had a significantly shorter duration of argatroban infusion compared with the warfarin group (3.8 days vs 11.2 days, respectively [P < .001]). Although hospital length of stay was numerically shorter with DOACs, the difference was not statistically significant. CONCLUSION AND RELEVANCE: In this study, transitioning to apixaban or rivaroxaban from argatroban for suspected or acute HIT was associated with a shorter duration of argatroban infusion. Application of this data may help reduce the duration of argatroban infusion for those with suspected or acute HIT being transitioned to oral anticoagulation.

articles.title: Clopidogrel in the Contemporary Management of Coronary and Cerebrovascular Events: Efficacy, Safety, and Decision-making Pathways.
articles.abstract: Clopidogrel (CLP) remains a cornerstone of antiplatelet therapy in the management of atherothrombotic events affecting the coronary and cerebrovascular circulations. As an irreversible thienopyridine inhibitor of the platelet P2Y12 adenosine diphosphate (ADP) receptor, CLP reduces platelet aggregation by preventing downstream activation of the glycoprotein IIb/IIIa receptor complex. It is a prodrug that requires hepatic bioactivation primarily via CYP2C19, resulting in susceptibility to pharmacogenomic variability and clinically significant drug-drug interactions. Current guidelines from the European Society of Cardiology (2023) and the American College of Cardiology/American Heart Association (2025) recommend potent P2Y12 inhibitors - ticagrelor and prasugrel - in preference to CLP for most patients with acute coronary syndromes (ACS) undergoing percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI); however, CLP retains a pivotal role when potent agents are contraindicated, in elderly patients at high bleeding risk (HBR), in cerebrovascular events, and as a de-escalation target following initial potent P2Y12 inhibition. In acute ischaemic stroke and high-risk TIA, short-course DAPT with CLP and aspirin for 21 days (not prolonged beyond this period) is the evidence-based standard of care. Major clinical trials - including CAPRIE, CURE, CHANCE, POINT, and the landmark CHANCE-2 - have defined the therapeutic boundaries and limitations of CLP-based dual antiplatelet therapy (DAPT). Bleeding remains the most clinically significant adverse effect, with gastrointestinal haemorrhage the most frequent site and intracranial haemorrhage the most feared complication. This review synthesises current evidence, incorporating recent meta-analyses and guideline updates, to provide a practical, evidence-based framework for clinicians regarding the use of CLP and comparator P2Y12 inhibitors in coronary and cerebrovascular disease.

articles.title: Computational Insights Into The Phytochemical Frontier: From Foundation To Discovery.
articles.abstract: Phytochemicals, derived from plants, encompass a wide range of bioactive compounds with significant therapeutic potential, paving the way for novel drug discoveries. While conventional experimental approaches have traditionally been used to study these compounds, the growing demand for safe and effective therapeutics has positioned computational methods as a transformative alternative. Computational approaches offer a promising avenue for efficient discovery and comprehensive analysis of bioactive phytochemicals, which may significantly reduce time and cost. The emergence and re-emergence of pathogens underscore the need for rapid therapeutic development, and computational approaches provide valuable support for phytochemical research. Understanding the available resources and their use will help advance therapeutics. Therefore, this review offers and highlights insights into phytochemicals and their integration with computational resources to deliver more accurate outcomes. It also highlights current advancements and challenges in computational phytochemical research, followed by an exploration of emerging AI-assisted techniques, including de novo compound design, predictive modelling, and network pharmacology. Additionally, it critically evaluates the strengths and limitations of computational resources and presents an optimal framework to help optimize and accelerate phytochemical discovery and therapeutic development, expanding their applications across scientific and industrial domains.

articles.title: Perspective on the Development of New Drugs for the Therapy of Thyroid Eye Disease.
articles.abstract: Thyroid Eye Disease (TED) is an autoimmune disease that affects the orbital extraocular tissues, characterized by inflammation of the extraocular tissue, causing proptosis and diplopia. Glucocorticoids, surgery and orbital radiation therapy are standard therapeutic strategies for moderate-severe TED; however, these treatments target the clinical symptoms and signs, but do not address the biological processes of the disease. In this context, therapies that target the immunopathogenic mechanisms underlying TED have been developed. The advent of Teprotumumab, a monoclonal antibody directed against the insulin-like growth factor 1 receptor (IGF-1R), capable of reducing both inflammation and orbital extraocular tissue remodeling, has represented a crucial step for the therapy of TED. Actually, several new drugs that target IGF-1R, B lymphocytes, neonatal Fc receptor, and cytokines have been developed, and they are being evaluated in clinical trials in TED patients. This perspective summarizes current targeted therapies and emerging approaches that may further improve the management of TED.
